explanation: eta photoproduction/electroproduction threshold on the proton is W_thr = m_p + m_eta = 0.938272 + 0.54786 = 1.486132 GeV (using the proton and eta masses hard-coded in exclurad.F's setcon subroutine). The requested W = 1.4885 GeV is only ~2.4 MeV above threshold, so the point is kinematically allowed (not refused) but sits in the most delicate part of the phase space: EXCLURAD's radiative photon phase-space variable vmax = W^2 - m_eta^2 + m_p^2 - 2*W*m_p works out to only ~0.0026 GeV^2 here, i.e. two orders of magnitude below the standard CLAS12 vcut of 0.166 GeV^2, so the code will silently fall back to using the full (tiny) vmax as the effective cut instead of the requested vcut. This is a real physics regime (S-wave threshold production, small Born cross section, small radiative tail) rather than a code bug, but it means: (1) the radiative correction factor can vary rapidly with W here and is more sensitive to interpolation error in the EtaMAID-2023 table (whose grid starts at W = 1.4856 GeV, so this point is still inside the tabulated range), and (2) near-zero phase space integrations are exactly the regime where the legacy NAG-library integrator historically reported ifail=2 errors (see the template's trailing sentinel line), so the output should be checked for a nonzero, finite radcor.dat/radtot.dat result before trusting it. Generated a single-point input file (model=3 EtaMAID, ivec=1 proton detected, bmom=6.53 GeV CLAS12, vcut=0.166 GeV^2 as usual -- it has no effect here since vmax < vcut) with W=1.4885 GeV, Q2=0.5 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0.2, phi*=60 deg. No corrections were applied to the requested kinematics themselves.
